name: Sweet-chili chicken breast (spray-fried, 1 kg base)

source.author: mako.co.il — 5-ingredient chicken breast in sweet chili sauce
source.notes: mako is egress-blocked by the network proxy, so the recipe was reconstructed from the identical 5-ingredient version (chicken dredged in flour, fried, tossed in sweet chili + honey/silan + soy) confirmed via web search. Built to the user's spec: 1 kg chicken breast and OLIVE-OIL SPRAY for frying instead of the original 4–5 tbsp of oil — that swap alone saves roughly 500 kcal / ~55 g fat off the whole dish. Analyzed for the whole batch; per_serving = batch ÷ 4. The sauce (sweet chili + soy) is the sugar/sodium lever. Estimate — sweet-chili sauces vary.

serving_desc: ≈220 g cooked (¼ of a 1 kg-chicken batch) — ~250 g raw chicken per serving

ingredients.note: shake off excess; can skip/reduce for fewer refined carbs
main added-sugar source; a low-sugar sweet chili cuts it a lot
the user's swap for 4–5 tbsp oil — big calorie save

steps: Cut the chicken; dredge lightly in flour and shake off the excess.
Spray a pan with olive oil, heat, and fry the chicken on both sides until golden and cooked through.
Mix the sweet chili, honey/silan and soy; pour into the pan and toss 1–2 min until the sauce coats the chicken and turns glossy. Serve.

batch_totals.note: Whole 1 kg-chicken dish, spray-fried. Deep-frying the original way (4–5 tbsp oil) would add ~500 kcal / ~55 g fat — the spray swap keeps total fat to ~29 g. The sauce carries ~91 g added sugar and ~4,600 mg sodium across the batch.

him.verdict: The lean-protein bones of this are excellent: ~59 g protein per serving for ~450 kcal (~13 g protein per 100 kcal!), and your olive-oil-spray swap is exactly right — it keeps fat to ~7 g/serving where deep-frying would have doubled the calories. The catch is entirely the sauce: sweet chili + honey push ~23 g added sugar per serving, and ¼ cup soy makes it ~1,150 mg sodium/serving. So it's a fantastic protein source wrapped in a sugary, salty glaze. Easy to fix without losing the flavor (see mods) — dial the sauce back and this is a 9.
flags: ~59 g protein / 450 kcal (~13 g protein per 100 kcal — outstanding)
spray-fried: only ~7 g fat/serving (vs ~2x calories deep-fried)
~23 g added sugar/serving from sweet chili + honey
flour dredge = a little refined carb; portion is large (~250 g raw chicken)
suggested_mods: Use LOW-SODIUM soy and cut it to ~2 tbsp — biggest sodium lever
Halve the sweet chili + skip the honey (or use a low-sugar sweet chili) — the chili flavor still carries; drops added sugar sharply
Skip or thin the flour dredge for fewer refined carbs; add garlic/ginger/chili flakes for flavor instead of sugar
Bulk it with stir-fried veg (peppers, broccoli, snap peas) — adds fiber + vitamin C and stretches the servings
Keep the olive-oil spray — that swap is already doing the heavy lifting

her_preconception.verdict: Lean, fully-cooked chicken is a solid protein + choline + selenium source for her with no safety flags — cook it through (74 °C, no pink) as standard. The downsides are the same as his: it's sugar- and sodium-heavy from the sauce (worth moderating in pregnancy), and it's not a big prenatal-micronutrient dish on its own. Great base; make it a winner by dialing back the sauce and serving it over vegetables for folate + vitamin C.

safety_advisories.note: Cook the chicken fully through (74 °C / no pink) — standard.

suggested_mods: Use low-sodium soy and less sweet chili to ease salt + sugar
Serve over a big veg/leafy side for folate, iron + vitamin C

cooking_guide: Cut the chicken into even strips or cubes so they cook at the same rate. Pat them DRY with paper towel and season with salt and pepper — dry surface is what lets them brown instead of steam.
Dredge lightly in flour and shake off the excess for a thin crust (or skip the flour for a lower-carb version).
Spray a nonstick pan with olive oil and heat over medium-high. Work in BATCHES — don't crowd the pan, or the chicken steams and goes grey instead of golden.
Sear the pieces undisturbed 2–3 min per side until deep golden and cooked through (74 °C, no pink). Set aside while you do the next batch.

Stir together the sweet chili, honey/silan and soy. Return all the chicken to the pan, pour the sauce over and toss 1–2 min on medium until it's glossy and clinging — don't go longer or the sugar scorches.
Finish with sesame and sliced scallions; serve over rice, noodles or stir-fried veg.

Lower sugar/sodium tips: use low-sodium soy, cut the sweet chili with a splash of water or rice vinegar, and lean on fresh garlic, ginger and chili flakes for flavor so you need less of the sweet glaze.
